mainTopic: Joining narrow cross-beams (לבוד versus חבוט רמי), shade versus sun in the סכך, very thick סכך, and a סוכה on a wagon, ship, tree or camel.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about cross-beams (קורות) over an alleyway (מבוי). The ברייתא covers beams that leave a gap and two thin beams lying side by side. It also covers two thin beams at different heights, which רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says we view as joined if both are between ten טפחים and twenty אמות. The גמרא infers from this that חבוט רמי works even for a beam less than a טפח wide, which challenges רבא. The answer rereads the ברייתא so that the beams are less than three טפחים apart and join through לבוד. The גמרא then sets two משניות against each other about a סוכה with equal shade and sun. It answers that one measures at the סכך above and the other on the floor below, and רב פפא backs this with a folk saying. A ברייתא next teaches that very thick סכך is kosher, and בית הלל allow it even when no sunlight comes through. Finally, a new משנה rules on a סוכה built on a wagon, ship, tree or camel. Each of these is kosher, but one may not go up into it on יום טוב if using it means relying on a tree or an animal.

steps.title: A gap of less than four needs no new beam
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its first case: a gap under four טפחים needs no extra beam, and a gap of four does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the gap is less than four טפחים, you do not need to bring another beam. If it is four, you do need to bring another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא that the גמרא started quoting on the previous amud. This line finishes the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on the first case, beams that do not reach across and leave a gap. His opinion began on the previous amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא, on the previous amud, allowed a gap only under three טפחים, the standard לבוד measure. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is more lenient and allows any gap under four טפחים. At four טפחים he agrees that a new beam is needed. The same two תנאים argue again about the next case, in steps 2 and 3.

keyTerms.meaning: A cross-beam placed over the entrance of an alleyway (מבוי) so that people may carry inside it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the beginning of the ברייתא. It started on the previous amud, so this line only finishes a case that was already set up.

phrases.english: Less than four [טפחים] —
phrases.notes: This is talking about the gap from the case that started on the previous amud.

phrases.english: one need not bring another beam;
four — one must bring another beam.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבָּעָה אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא קוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא quoted on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a gap of less than four טפחים does not require a new beam, and a gap of four does. The תנא קמא allows less than three.

steps.title: Two thin beams side by side combine to hold a half-brick
steps.stepSummary: Two narrow parallel beams count together if, combined, they can hold an אריח along its width of one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, two parallel beams: neither one alone is wide enough to hold a half-brick. If together they can hold the half-brick along its width of one טפח, you do not need another beam. If not, you need another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a new case: two skinny beams lying next to each other, neither wide enough by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valid קורה must be wide enough to hold an אריח, a half-brick that measures one טפח by three. Here each beam is too thin, but we combine them. If together they can hold the brick along its narrow side of one טפח, they count as one good beam.

keyTerms.meaning: Parallel beams, lying next to each other
A half-brick, one טפח wide and three טפחים long

phrases.english: And similarly, two parallel beams,
there is not enough in this one to hold a half-brick
and not enough in that one to hold a half-brick,
if together they can hold a half-brick along its width, one טפח —
one need not bring another beam,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא קוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת,
phrases.english: and if not — one must bring another beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two thin parallel beams combine if together they can hold an אריח along its one-טפח width.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires three טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the two beams must hold the אריח along its length of three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if they can hold a half-brick along its length of three טפחים, you do not need another beam. If not, you need another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees about how wide the combined beams must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא is satisfied with one טפח, the brick's width. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wants the beams to hold the brick lengthwise, which takes three טפחים. Both opinions agree that the two beams may combine. They argue only about the size required.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מְקַבְּלוֹת אָרִיחַ לְאׇרְכּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים —
phrases.english: if they can hold a half-brick along its length, three handbreadths —
one need not bring another beam.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא קוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: And if not — one must bring another beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the required size in the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the combined beams must hold the אריח along its three-טפח length.

steps.title: Beams at different heights are viewed as if brought together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules that if one beam is higher and one lower, we imagine them joined at the same level.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one beam was above and one below, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: we view the upper one as if it were below, and the lower one as if it were above.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a harder case: the two thin beams are not at the same height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the beams are separated vertically, we imagine them pushed toward each other, so the top one comes down and the bottom one goes up. If together they would hold the brick, they count as one beam. This idea of imagining the upper beam lowered is the same concept the גמרא calls חבוט רמי.

keyTerms.meaning: We view it as if; we imagine

phrases.english: If they were one above and one below,
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
we view the upper one as though it were below,
and the lower one as though it were above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the side-by-side case to beams at different heights
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beams at different heights are viewed as joined together.

steps.title: Both beams must stay within the valid height range
steps.stepSummary: The upper beam may not be above twenty אמות, and the lower beam may not be below ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only if the upper beam is not above twenty אמות, and the lower beam is not below ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds a condition to his rule. This condition is the line the גמרא will draw its inference from in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam over a מבוי only works between ten טפחים and twenty אמות off the ground. So both beams must sit inside that range for us to imagine them joined. The ברייתא names the height limits as the only condition. It says nothing about how wide the upper beam must be.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty cubits, the maximum valid height

phrases.english: provided that the upper one is not
above twenty cubits,
and the lower one not below ten [טפחים].

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא עֶלְיוֹנָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joining the beams works only when both are between ten טפחים and twenty אמות high.

steps.title: Inference: lowering works even without a handbreadth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that within twenty אמות we say חבוט רמי even when the upper beam is less than a טפח wide, which challenges רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if both beams are within twenty אמות, we say 'push it down' even though the upper beam is not a טפח wide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא for its real purpose: it reads an inference from it and uses that inference to challenge רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each beam in this case is too thin, less than a טפח. Yet the ברייתא still lets us imagine the upper one lowered, as long as it is under twenty אמות. That contradicts רבא, who holds that חבוט רמי only applies when the upper beam is at least a טפח wide.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Push it down and place it': we imagine the higher item lowered into position
We say; we apply the principle

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lets two too-thin beams at different heights combine through חבוט רמי. That suggests the upper beam does not need a טפח of width, which is a difficulty for רבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next stage of the sugya: whether, and how, רבא can explain this ברייתא.

phrases.english: This implies that when both are within twenty —
we say 'push it down and place it,'

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ טֶפַח!
phrases.english: even though it does not have a handbreadth!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא זֶה וְזֶה בְּתוֹךְ עֶשְׂרִים אָמְרִינַן חֲבוֹט רְמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the condition in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that חבוט רמי requires the upper beam to be a טפח wide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא applies the lowering idea to beams that are each too thin, and names height as the only limit. So a טפח of width is not required.

steps.title: Reread the ברייתא: the beams are joined by לבוד
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread so that the two beams are within twenty אמות and less than three טפחים apart. They join through לבוד, not through חבוט רמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Fix the wording and read it like this. As long as the upper beam is not above twenty, but is inside twenty, and the lower beam is close to it, less than three טפחים away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge against רבא. He does this by giving the ברייתא a new meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that the ברייתא uses חבוט רמי even for an upper beam narrower than a טפח. The answer says the two beams are less than three טפחים apart, so לבוד joins them. No 'pushing down' is needed, and רבא's rule stays safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Fix it and read it like this (a rereading of the source)
A gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'within twenty' is not proof of חבוט רמי. Here the beams are joined only because they are so close to each other (לבוד).

phrases.english: He said to him: Fix it and say it like this:
phrases.notes: He's reading the ברייתא a different way, to defend רבא.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא עֶלְיוֹנָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים,
phrases.english: Provided that the upper beam is not above twenty,
but rather within twenty,
and the lower one is close to it, less than three טפחים away.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא (a new case setup)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא uses חבוט רמי even for a narrow upper beam.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is a case of לבוד, with the beams less than three טפחים apart.

steps.title: Second rereading: the lower beam is above ten
steps.stepSummary: Another way to read the ברייתא: the lower beam is above ten טפחים and the upper beam is within three טפחים of it. If they are three apart, there is no חבוט רמי, because the beam is less than a טפח wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else: As long as the lower beam is not below ten, but is above ten, and the upper beam is close to it, less than three away. But if they are three apart, since the beam is not a טפח wide, we do not say חבוט רמי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to reread the ברייתא. It ends by stating the rule clearly: a beam less than a טפח wide is not 'pushed down.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the focus is on the lower beam, but the idea is the same: the beams join through לבוד. The closing line matches רבא exactly. A beam narrower than a טפח is not pushed down, so beams three or more טפחים apart do not join.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Push it down': we picture the upper beam lowered to the level of the lower one
Since it is not a טפח wide

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, חבוט רמי only works for a beam at least a טפח wide. Narrower beams can join only through לבוד, meaning less than three טפחים apart.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: בִּלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא תַּחְתּוֹנָה לְמַטָּה מֵעֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.english: Alternatively: provided that the lower beam is not below ten,
but rather above ten,
and the upper one is close to it, less than three away,
but if they are three apart,
since it does not have a טפח of width —
we do not say 'push it down.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same קשיא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The beams join by לבוד. With no full טפח, there is no חבוט רמי.

steps.title: משנה: more shade than sun is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, which says a סוכה with more shade than sun is kosher. From this it infers that if they are equal, the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one whose shade is more than its sun is kosher. This implies: if they are equal, it is פסולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה and draws an inference from it. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only names 'more shade' as kosher. That suggests an exactly equal amount of shade and sun is not good enough.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies: if they are equal

phrases.english: And one whose shade is greater than its sun is kosher.
This implies that if they are equal, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: More shade means kosher. The inference is that equal shade and sun means פסולה.

steps.title: Contradiction with the other chapter's משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in the first פרק says more sun than shade is פסולה. That implies equal shade and sun is kosher, which contradicts step 9.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the other chapter: one whose sun is more than its shade is פסולה. This implies: if they are equal, it is kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the two משניות against each other. Each one suggests the opposite ruling for the case of equal shade and sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה implies that equal is פסולה. The משנה in the first פרק implies that equal is kosher. Both cannot be true about the same סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the other chapter:
and one whose sun is greater than its shade is invalid,
this implies that if they are equal, it is kosher!

steps.kashyaTarget: What the law is when shade and sun are equal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two משניות imply opposite rulings for the same case.

steps.title: Measured at the roof versus on the floor
steps.stepSummary: Each משנה measures in a different place: one at the סכך above, the other on the floor below.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it means above, and there it means below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the two משניות are measuring in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sunlight spreads out as it falls. So gaps in the סכך look bigger on the floor than they really are up top. If shade and sun look equal on the floor, the סכך itself must really have more covering than gaps, so it is kosher. If they are equal up at the roof itself, it is פסולה.
steps.whatToRemember: Equal shade and sun at the roof is פסולה. Equal shade and sun on the floor is kosher.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here, it means from above,
there, it means from below.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different places where the measuring is done)
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about the roof. The other משנה is about the floor.

steps.title: רב פפא's folk saying about light
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא supports the answer with a saying: a gap the size of a זוז above shows up the size of an איסתרא below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: Like a זוז above, like an איסתרא below.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings an everyday saying that backs up the previous answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסתרא is a larger coin than a זוז. The saying shows that light spreads out and looks bigger by the time it reaches the floor. This is exactly why 'equal' on the floor means less than equal at the roof.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said,
this is what people say:
like a זוז above, like an איסתרא below.

steps.raayaObject: That light spreads out and looks bigger lower down.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying quoted by רב פפא.

steps.title: Thick סכך: stars not visible is still kosher
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a סוכה whose סכך is as thick as a house roof is kosher even if the stars cannot be seen through it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Thick like a house.' The Rabbis taught: One that is thick like a house, even though the stars cannot be seen from inside it, is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. It then brings a ברייתא that explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being able to see the stars is ideal, but it is not required. Thick סכך does not make the סוכה פסולה.

phrases.english: 'Thick like a type of house.'
The Rabbis taught: One that is thick like a type of house,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַכּוֹכָבִים נִרְאִין מִתּוֹכָהּ —
phrases.english: even though the stars are not seen from inside it —
it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thick סכך through which the stars cannot be seen is kosher.

steps.title: No sunbeams get through: בית שמאי versus בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: If even rays of sunlight cannot get through, בית שמאי say the סוכה is פסולה and בית הלל say it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the sun's rays cannot be seen from inside it, בית שמאי say it is פסולה and בית הלל say it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with an even thicker case, where there is a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the סכך is so thick that no sunlight at all comes through. בית שמאי think it is too much like a regular house. בית הלל still accept it, which matches our משנה's word 'kosher.'

keyTerms.meaning: Rays of the sun (literally 'stars of the sun')

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows בית הלל: even סכך that blocks all sunlight is kosher.

phrases.english: if the rays of the sun are not seen from inside it —
Beit Shammai rule it invalid
and Beit Hillel rule it kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a more extreme case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When no sunlight gets through, בית שמאי say פסולה and בית הלל say kosher.

steps.title: A סוכה on top of a wagon or a ship
steps.stepSummary: A סוכה built on a wagon or a ship is kosher, and you may go up into it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone builds his סוכה on top of a wagon or on top of a ship, it is kosher, and he may go up into it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It rules that a סוכה on a wagon or ship is kosher, and you may use it even on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה only has to be a temporary home, so a moving base like a wagon or ship does not make it פסולה. There is also no rabbinic ban on climbing onto a wagon or ship, so nothing stops you from going up on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
One may go up into it, meaning one may use it
The festival day itself, here the first day of סוכות

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who makes his sukka
at the top of the wagon
or at the top of the ship
it is kosher, and one may go up into it on the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves from the thickness of the סכך (steps 13-14) to a new topic: where the סוכה is placed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה on a wagon or ship is kosher and may be used on יום טוב.

steps.title: A סוכה on top of a tree or a camel
steps.stepSummary: A סוכה on a tree or camel is kosher, but you may not go up into it on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he builds it at the top of a tree or on top of a camel, it is kosher, but he may not go up into it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. The סוכה is still kosher, but using it on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוכה itself is fine. The problem is that חכמים forbade using a tree or riding an animal on יום טוב. Going up into this סוכה would mean using the tree or camel. So the סוכה is kosher, but on יום טוב it cannot be used. On חול המועד it may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: But one may not go up into it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'may not go up' as meaning the סוכה is פסולה. The משנה says clearly that it is כשרה. The only problem is a separate יום טוב rule against using trees and animals.

phrases.english: at the top of a tree
or on top of a camel
it is kosher,
but one may not go up into it on the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי גָּמָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a contrast with step 15. Both סוכות are kosher, but only the wagon or ship סוכה may be used on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה on a tree or camel is kosher, but using it on יום טוב is forbidden because of the rabbinic ban on using trees and animals.

steps.title: A סוכה that is partly held up by a tree
steps.stepSummary: Two walls in the tree and one made by a person, or the reverse, is kosher, but it may not be used on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two walls are in the tree and one is made by a person, or two are made by a person and one is in the tree, it is kosher, but one may not go up into it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a mixed case. Some walls rest on a tree and some are built on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה needs at least three walls. Here the tree is one of the walls that makes up that minimum, so the סוכה depends on the tree. Using the סוכה therefore means using the tree, which is forbidden on יום טוב. The סוכה itself is still kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Made by a person, built on the ground

phrases.english: two walls in the tree
and one made by a person,
or two made by a person
and one in the tree

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁרָה, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: it is kosher, but one may not go up into it on the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the tree rule from step 16 to a סוכה that rests only partly on a tree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the tree is needed to complete the required walls, the סוכה is kosher but may not be used on יום טוב.

steps.title: Three man-made walls and one in the tree
steps.stepSummary: With three walls built by a person and one in the tree, the סוכה is kosher and may be used on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If three walls are made by a person and one is in the tree, it is kosher, and one may go up into it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case where the tree is not needed. Here using the סוכה on יום טוב is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three walls built by a person already give the minimum number of walls. The סוכה could stand as a kosher סוכה even if the tree were taken away. So the tree is only extra, and using the סוכה does not count as using the tree.
steps.whatToRemember: Every סוכה in this משנה is כשרה. The יום טוב question is separate: if using the סוכה means relying on a tree or an animal, it is forbidden on יום טוב. If the tree is only extra, it is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea of the משנה. Whether a סוכה is כשרה and the rules of יום טוב are two separate tests, and the second test depends on whether the tree is actually needed.

phrases.english: three made by a person
and one in the tree
it is kosher, and one may go up into it on the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 17. Once three walls are built by a person, the tree is no longer needed, so the יום טוב ban does not apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When three man-made walls are enough without the tree, the סוכה is kosher and may be used on יום טוב.
